title: Roads in Bagepalli
body: Bagepalli is a small town near Bengaluru. Some government officials decided that the town would be better off with double roads and streetlights. The work was carried out in a very unprofessional manner. Traffic movement became difficult and there were numerous accidents. A local citizen then used the Right to Information Act to ask for information about the money allocated for the roadwork. With this information in hand, a group of citizens met and questioned the officials concerned. The officials later ensured that the roadwork was completed to the satisfaction of all concerned.

title: A rule in an apartment complex
body: A Resident Welfare Association (RWA) of an apartment complex banned all deliveries after 9 pm. The rule was passed by a majority vote. A smaller group of residents had argued that the ban would hurt the sick and the elderly, but their view was ignored. One night, an elderly resident collapsed because of low blood sugar; the medicine she needed could not be delivered to her flat in time. After this, the RWA changed its rule so that food and medicines were no longer covered by the ban.
